steps.content: [Background: Mountain Woods in Eastia]
From that day onward, the young girl visited the injured child each time she ascended the mountain to forage for herbs.

She spoke to the child often. A word or two might come in answer, but usually the child just stared and listened, eyes luminous and untamed, like the wild beasts the girl had encountered on those same slopes.

As the days wore on, the child's defenses lowered. There was no more squirming when the bandages were changed, and occasionally the child crept a little closer, drawn by curiosity as the girl pulled one strange thing after another from her bag.

The child watched in bewilderment as the girl drew a length of red string from her bag. With practiced hands, she tied it carefully around the child's wrist. Unused to the feel of anything against her skin, the child shook her arm several times, but the string held fast. In the end, she simply gave up.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: This is a protective charm. I went all the way to the Mountain Lord's temple just for this.
The girl lifted her hand, and there around her own wrist lay an identical string. Against the endless white of the snow, that slash of red seemed to burn with particular intensity.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: This place used to be a temple too, though it had fewer worshippers than the one down the mountain. Anyone who walks White Tiger Mountain wears one of these. If your heart is true, the White Tiger Mountain Lord keeps you safe. No harm will come to you here.
White... Tiger...?

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: That's right. See? Now the Mountain Lord watches over you, too.

The hand that bore the red string moved gently over the child's crown, taming the wild locks and plaiting them into a neat braid. The child's ears flickered with hesitation, but she did not draw back.
Another day slipped by. The girl had yet to show herself on the mountain.
More than half a month had gone by. The child's injured leg had nearly mended. She could have long since returned to her cave across the mountain, yet she remained.
The child crouched in the grass outside the ruined temple, then scrambled up onto the roof beneath the shade of the tree. She lay down, drifted off, rolled over several times, then sat up once more.
The girl was late again today. The sun had already set. The child touched her nearly-healed leg, and at last, made up her mind to leave—
[Background: Any Eastian mountain path from event backgrounds]

She passed several old, sickly wolves. Their pack had long since forsaken them, yet hunger drove them to circle a young deer with a broken leg. The mother deer stood firm between her fawn and the predators, hooves raking the earth in mute warning.

She passed a hunter whose eyes had long gone dark. He hunched low in the underbrush, a crude crossbow held in his hands, patient as stone. Across the clearing, a wild boar rooted contentedly among the fallen fruit, deaf to the fate coiling nearby.

She passed a robbery unfolding on the road. Faced with the glint of bandits' blades, a figure had thrown their arms wide, a living barrier between the knives and the trembling mother and daughter huddled at their back.
...Huh?
The child finally stopped in her tracks.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: Don't be afraid! They just want money. They won't dare hurt anyone. People from town will come soon... They'll drive these scoundrels away!

The bandits erupted in laughter. Sweat traced a path down the girl's temple, yet she held her ground. Only when one of them lunged forward to tear the child from the mother's grasp did her composure finally crack.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: Don't touch her—Ah!
Blades came down in a shower toward her. The girl choked back a scream, jaw locked tight and eyes pressed shut.
[2-second sequence with clash sounds as someone blocks the attack]

steps.speaker: Bandit
steps.content: Aaahhh!

A small figure caught the hurtling axe with nothing but a bare hand, then shattered the wielder's joints as if snapping dry twigs. Claws raked across a throat. The man reeled backward, hands flying to his neck, and crumpled to the ground.
Enraged, the others swung their weapons toward the child.

Clang. Claws met iron in a shriek of grinding steel. She slipped between the bandits like a wraith, every motion carving crimson arcs through the frozen air. The snow beneath them bloomed red. Some turned and fled, while others dropped to their knees, pleading. It made no difference.
The slaughter ended as swiftly as it had begun. The bandits lay sprawled in spreading pools. She shook out her hands with a flicker of irritation, annoyed by the slick warmth clinging to her skin.
Then she remembered why she had intervened at all. She turned to see if the ones she had shielded were unharmed—
And found only terror staring back at her.

The girl sagged where she knelt before the mother and daughter, hands still quivering from the shock. Yet the fear burning in her gaze had found a new target; it clung now to the small figure standing amid the spreading blood.
The child took a step toward her. The girl's whole body jerked back, a violent, involuntary recoil, as if some primal instinct screamed at her to retreat.

steps.speaker: Terrified Child
steps.content: ...Monster! Stay away!!

A stone landed at her feet. The child who threw it was pulled behind the mother, her face drained of color, and the girl, their bodies forming a barrier between the small one and the "thing" they now feared most.
[Flashback Segment]

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: Anyone who walks White Tiger Mountain wears one of these. If your heart is true, the White Tiger Mountain Lord keeps you safe. No harm will come to you here.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: That's right. See? Now the Mountain Lord watches over you, too.
[Back to present]
"The White Tiger Mountain Lord keeps you safe. No harm will come to you here." But who would they protect? And from whose harm?
Monster... is... me?

Her throat tightened, dry and choked. Her chest ached as though a boulder had settled upon it. She did not know this feeling. She knew only that the air had grown impossibly cold, and that the red string on her wrist burned like fire against her skin.
She ripped it from her wrist and flung it to the earth. Still bright, barely worn, it was now smudged with dirt.
Jichuan
[Bureau]
Xiaofeng lies sprawled across a sun-drenched platform, rolling over with listless boredom.

A rare dream of the past is souring her mood, though she is too lazy to bother venting. After spending so long surrounded by steel and concrete, she finds herself missing her den deep in the mountains.

The MBCC recreation yard is spacious enough; Sinners gather in small clusters while high walls and wire mesh gleam with an almost surreal softness in the sunlight. Distant voices of other Sinners drift over, but to her, it is nothing but noise.
An enormous tiger head nudges in from the side. Purring, the white tiger nuzzles into her palm, then mirrors her posture and settles down beside her, its tail curling around her feet.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tch... Meowy, when we ditch this dump, you wanna eat first or nap first?
The tiger offers no answer, just a purr that grows louder.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Hmph. You lazy furball...
The wire mesh overhead is nothing but an eyesore, sealing off any route of escape, but Xiaofeng can't muster the will to care. It all feels so pointless.
She drifts back to her spot and lets her eyes fall shut under the warmth of the sun, waiting for the team due to escort her back to Eastia. However...
A verse says thus! At Hundred Treasures Peak's winding turn, the tiger veils its sacred form. The mortal world fears what it cannot know, a divine heart, forever scorned!
A child's bright voice rings out suddenly from below the platform. Xiaofeng cracks an eye open and spots a figure waving a lion head mask in the air.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Ladies and gentlemen! Today, I won't regale you with tales of the Rust's 108 Forbidden Acts, nor the epic of the three Campbell siblings! No. Today, I speak of a legendary Eastian mountain! And that mountain is—

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: White... White-something Mountain!

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: How's a cage this small stuffed with this many people... Can't even catch a damn nap around here...

Grumbling beneath her breath, Xiaofeng rolls onto her side, clamps her hands over her ears, and buries her face deep in the tiger's fur, trying desperately to drown out the swell of cheers and applause from below.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hello, everyone! I am the super-duper mega ultra spectacular incredible amazing undefeated supreme Lion Dancing Queen—umm, whatever-number-generation successor! OwO!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Today, I bring you an all-new production, Tale of Descending the Mountain, also known as Legend of the Tiger Deity! Anyone who wants to join in, hop on up! Show me that fire!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Director! Question!
EMP leaps onto the stage first. In her hands, she clutches pages that might generously pass for a script, squinting at the messy handwriting while stumbling her way through the performance.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: If it's a tiger but also a deity... like, tigers eat people and deities save people. That's totally contradictory. What gives?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Ah, patience, dear audience! Allow me to explain in due time.

Legends whisper of a sacred mountain deep within the wilds of Eastia. Where tigers stalked the crags and virgin snow crowned the summit. That place was the White Tiger Mountain. An unbroken veil of mystic mist clung to its heights. Below, villagers prostrated themselves, burning fragrant incense toward the unseen peak, beseeching the mountain's mighty spirit for sanctuary.

Their earnest devotion bore wondrous fruit. When wolves slunk close beneath the moon, a tiger's thunderous roar shattered the silence, scattering the pack like leaves. When children lost their footing on sheer drops, unseen gales cradled them softly back to earth.

This mountain deity was both just and benevolent. Though their visage remained forever hidden, their hand moved only in grace. Present your finest wines and warmest welcome, and the deity's favor is assured.
The woman curled on the platform flicks her ears, and her body shifts instinctively toward the sound of the voices.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: But one day, disaster struck the village! Little EMP ventured out to buy supplies for the New Year festivities, only to encounter... mountain bandits!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Uhh... Go, go! Bandit time!

Lightning-quick, EMP snatches hold of Ninety-Nine, who has been swinging her sword in practice nearby, and hauls her into the unfolding scene. Ninety-Nine blinks in confusion, then gestures toward herself.

steps.speaker: Ninety-Nine
steps.content: Me?

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: YES, you! Make it convincing!
Following a barrage of theatrical winks and overblown gestures from EMP, Ninety-Nine reluctantly takes the script and starts to read.

steps.speaker: Ninety-Nine
steps.content: Your money or your life. Empty your pockets. Coins, bills, all of it. Or else...
The heavy greatsword slices a clean arc through the air, then plunges into the ground with a ringing clang.

steps.speaker: Ninety-Nine
steps.content: Consider yourselves dead!

A beat of silence passes before the crowd erupts. Some reel backward with dramatic flair; others dive for cover, hands clamped over their heads. Screams ricochet across the room. Their acting abilities may range from passable to hopeless, but every last one of them throws themselves into the role of a terrified villager.
Xiaofeng turns her head, her gaze locking onto the scene below.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Uh... candy? Nope. Gone. Ate it all. And my DisCoins... you've been holding those, right? I got nothing! Zip! Zero!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Oh Mountain Lord, Mountain Lord! Hear my prayer! I'll offer you all my snacks! Years' worth! They're stashed under the beanbag cushions! Chi—I mean, the village chief worked so hard sneaking those in for me. I've been hoarding them forever!
She presses her hands together, and her voice shifts into something unexpectedly reverent, as though she is channeling every last drop of desperation into her improvised rambling.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Ninety-Nine, I mean, such a kind bandit will totally let us go... right?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: No, no, no! The bandit is SUPER! MEGA! ULTRA! FURIOUS! You won't fork over a single thing?! Time to teach you a lesson!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Bandit, attack!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ???? Wait—WAIT—you're for REAL?!

Ninety-Nine brings the greatsword down exactly as instructed. EMP scrambles backward in pure panic, her lines dissolving into wordless shrieks. She plows straight into the crowd of spectators, and bodies go tumbling in every direction. The scene descends into utter chaos.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: MOUNTAIN LORD! MOUNTAIN LORD, SAVE ME! NINETY-NINE'S GONNA KILL ME—AAAHHH!
The greatsword slices through the air until a figure slips between them. Metal collides with metal. A shower of sparks erupts.

Xiaofeng catches Ninety-Nine's greatsword in one hand, feet rooted to the ground. She rides the momentum forward, leaning in close and flashing a wicked grin. A flick of her wrist sends the blade aside, and the next strike meets the same casual deflection.

steps.speaker: Ninety-Nine
steps.content: Hyah!

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Well, well! You got some bite! C'mon, keep it coming!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Mountain Lord! You came! I got your back! Get her! Get her!

For all her talk, EMP stays well clear of the brawl's center, firing arrows from the safety of the sidelines. Her aim, unfortunately, proves less than stellar as stray shots find other Sinners among the crowd.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...! You...! Chief said no fighting!
Now locked in combat with Hecate, Xiaofeng finds she cannot disengage—the white tiger and the Nightmare, one tumbling through open air, the other darting swift and low.

Around them, the other Sinners are either swept into the chaos or hurl themselves into it headlong. The air rings with laughter, shouts, and the crashing din of bodies and blades meeting. Shockwaves roll across the yard in quick succession, each burst of force held carefully in check.

Xiaofeng gives herself over to the fight. Her strikes come faster, her laughter rises freer. For a breath, she is no longer here; she is back in the deep forests of Eastia's mountains, moving on instinct alone, untamed and wild as the tiger she has always been.
Until the final blow lands, and the last clash echoes into stillness. One by one, the exhausted fighters drop to the ground.
Heavy breathing mingles with scattered laughter and breathless swearing. The brawl settles into a warm, weary quiet, and with it, the tale of the Tiger Deity nears its ending.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: At last, with the Mountain Lord's aid, the villagers returned home safely, New Year supplies in hand! The village chief, who had waited so anxiously, prepared a gift of gratitude for the Mountain Lord!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: From that day forth, below the Hundred Treasures Peak, some glimpsed children playing beside a white tiger. Others saw villagers shading the Mountain Lord with leaves. Villains gave the place a wide berth... and peace settled over the village. Forevermore!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: And so the tale concludes! All beings don mere mortal guises, yet compassion reveals the divine. The fierce tiger needs no solemn bearing, for within beats a hero's heart!
Xiaofeng lies sprawled on the ground. When she looks up, she finds someone crouching beside her, a tray in hand.
Pleasure's all mine, Tiger Deity.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: You...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: And that's a wrap! Everyone killed it! Especially YOU, the lady who played the White Tiger Mountain Lord!

OwO shoves through the crowd and bounds straight up to Xiaofeng, circling her with careful, meticulous attention. She studies everything: the ears, the tail, every last detail. Her eyes gleam with undisguised wonder.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Pretty slick, little one. I've caught storytellers and operas at the mountain's foot for years, but you're the first one who actually made me wanna jump in and stir things up myself.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hehe... I heard all those White Tiger Mountain stories from folks back in Goldionville! Never thought they'd be real! And I never dreamed I'd get to make a movie with the actual Mountain Lord herself! This is my first time seeing a real tiger up close!
Not far away, Meowy stands encircled by a cluster of curious Sinners. OwO, having secured permission, darts over with her camera in hand, eager to snap a few close-ups of the great tiger.
And as for the white tiger's master... Xiaofeng makes her way toward you, hands clasped loosely behind her back, her eyes narrowing with a glint of knowing intent.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Didn't you say I was utterly vicious? Needed to be kept under strict watch? Tch. What a load. Aren't you scared the spirits will crawl out at night and get you for lying to kids like that?
Well... I wouldn't call it a lie. Exactly.
After that day... I had a few friends in Eastia poke around for me. Tracked down some folks from the villages near White Tiger Mountain.

Just like you said, that Mountain Lord legend's been around forever. Nobody knows exactly when White Tiger Mountain or the Tiger Deity first showed up, but the stories haven't gone anywhere. If anything, the last ten years or so, people are telling them more than ever.
Hunters who work those mountains told me something interesting. They leave food at the Mountain Lord's shrine all the time. And those offerings...
You offer Xiaofeng the jerky from the tray, and catch the brief flicker of surprise that lifts her brows.
I got a feeling the Mountain Lord takes what's offered and keeps an eye out. Makes sure they all get home safe.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...What's your game? You try to trick me into running my mouth?
Not really. Just saying, this Mountain Lord seems like the soft type. All bark, no bite.

Xiaofeng offers no reply. She takes the jerky and begins to gnaw at it, grumbling what you can only assume are Eastian curses beneath her breath. The sight of her—cheeks full, still muttering—pulls an involuntary smile from you.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: What? You want me to smack you?
Nah. I was just thinking. About that question you asked the other day.
Why not just live free and easy?
For me... it's kinda like how people feel about the White Tiger Mountain Lord. The way they believe in them and trust them. I've also got people who care about me, people who expect things from me.
It's heavy sometimes. Yeah. But... for the ones who believe in me, I'll carry it.
You meet Xiaofeng's eyes.
Maybe it's the same for the Mountain Lord. Doesn't mean you gotta get all tangled up with everyone. Maybe it's just... you grab an offering when you're passing by and lend a hand when it's easy.
Even if you're not really thinking about it... to the folks living down below, that's a miracle. A god reaching down and touching their lives.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tch. Sappy nonsense.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Ugh, I knew we'd never see eye to eye. You humans are all the same. Maybe you can't throw a punch worth a damn, but every single one of you can talk circles around anyone. One slip and I walk right into it...

Xiaofeng polishes off the last piece of jerky, brushes her hands clean, and rises to her feet. You cannot see her face, but those fluffy ears of hers twitch once, then again. You swallow any teasing words before they can escape. You have finally reached this "deity," and you refuse to undo that now.
Together, you walk with Xiaofeng toward the edge of the venue, where Nightingale stands waiting.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, the ship back to Eastia is ready.

Xiaofeng summons the white tiger to her side. The majestic creature takes its place behind her, its fur now decorated with seven or eight red strings—bright little knots tied by the eager hands of a few young Sinners. The effect is at once regal and completely absurd.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: What? You jealous? Wanna tie one on yourself? Something to remember us by in case you miss us.
You step forward, but rather than tying something on, you toss a bundle her way. Xiaofeng catches it without effort.
Then, Mountain Lord, please watch over me from now on.
I'll pass. The Mountain Lord's protection's a little too good. I'd need to give a way better offering.
You step forward, but rather than tying something on, you toss a bundle her way. Xiaofeng catches it without effort.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: This is...?
It's silvervine branches. You have had them gathered specially—whole stems, still intact, tied together in a neat bundle with red string.
Consider it a keepsake. Take the main road next time, okay? This visit was too rushed. I couldn't show you around properly. But DisCity's got plenty worth seeing.
Besides, you like stories, right? Operas? I've picked up a few over the years. Why settle for secondhand when you can hear them straight from the source?
So... if you ever feel like swinging by DisCity again, come find me. Anywhere you wanna go, I'll show you.
Xiaofeng hesitates for just a moment. She offers no words, but after a few strides, her hand lifts in a lazy wave over her shoulder. That's her own way of saying goodbye.
The bundle of silvervine swings at her side, and the little golden tiger claw on her pinky sways with the motion, catching the light and scattering it in brief, bright glimmers.
A tiger's roar rings out as the golden gleam fades along with her retreating silhouette. You know exactly what she means:
Until we meet again.
[Flashback Fragment: Market Below the Mountain]
The sun danced in her cup, the light rippling with a gentle tremor. She had been staring at it for a while now.

This was her first time descending to the world below. She'd heard the girl speak of this place often enough, but that was years ago now, before the bitterness of their parting had settled in. She hadn't been back to the White Tiger Temple since that day, and she hadn't seen that herb-gathering girl again.

The food on the mountain was bland, and no matter how carefully she tried, she could never get the meat to sear quite right. Eventually, she'd decided to throw on her cloak and go down, slipping into the human market just to scratch that particular itch.

The mortal world buzzed around her, a thicket of overlapping chatter. In the span of a glance, she knocked back a mouthful of liquor and propped her head in her hand, listening to the spinning of yet another tall tale.

steps.speaker: Villager 1
steps.content: I heard that the tiger came right off the mountain and ripped those bandits to shreds! Ate 'em up, one by one! Tsk, tsk, tsk... Blood everywhere, nasty stuff!

steps.speaker: Villager 2
steps.content: Shh! Keep your voice down, will ya? The gods are always watching, and the White Tiger Temple's right there! You're gonna bring a curse down on us, bad-mouthing the Mountain Lord like that...

steps.speaker: Villager 1
steps.content: Hey, it's a tiger! Tigers eat folks. That's just how it goes! But you gotta admit, the trails up there have been way safer lately. Do you think...
She let out a short scoff and washed the last bite of meat down with her liquor. She was just pushing back from the table when a familiar voice cut through the din.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: That's a load of nonsense! The deity would never eat people!

steps.speaker: Villager 1
steps.content: Wha—you... Don't go spouting off, girl. What, you see it happen yourself or something?

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: Yeah! I did see it myself!
The girl, usually so gentle of speech, abruptly lifted her voice. Never before had she spoken with such volume; though it quavered, she compelled it to steadiness.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: It was her... The Tiger Deity saved me! She chased off those thieving scoundrels. The White Tiger Mountain Lord's not just some old story. She's real, and she's a real deity!

steps.speaker: Villager 2
steps.content: But... it's still a tiger...

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: Who cares if she's got fur or not! If she's doing good and saving folks, then she's a proper deity!

The girl stubbornly pressed on with her argument. Meanwhile, the figure beneath the cloak pursed her lips slightly and rose amid the commotion, only to be halted by the restaurant owner demanding payment.

steps.speaker: Restaurant Owner
steps.content: Let's see here... one plate of marinated beef, two cups of liquor... that'll be one qian of silver! Say, I don't recognize your face. You got a name, traveler?
The cloaked figure stopped short.
Her eyes found the White Tiger Temple at the entrance, where incense offerings had been thriving these days. A cluster of villagers moved to and fro, fixing a new couplet above the gate.

She let out a soft chuckle. The flowing black characters on the red paper meant nothing to her. She could not read a single stroke, but she had heard people recite the words before, whenever she slipped down the mountain for a taste of liquor.
Untamed roar echoes across the peaks for those who pray. The mountain lord guards all who dwell below, where the gale reach.
It honored the Tiger Deity, the Mountain Lord.
What a shame, then, that no such deity guarded those heights. Deep in the mountains there was only a white tiger, and a woman the tiger had raised, mistaken by all for the Mountain Lord.

Humans fascinated her. So fragile, so fleeting—barely able to cling to life on their own—so they prayed to gods and ghosts, begging for a helping hand. And yet they never begged for much. They just handed their wishes and their hopes over to something bigger than themselves.
"Not seeking glory or a name in history, only peace, good fortune, and a life free of worry."

Wish after wish, prayer after prayer, they braided themselves together. They took shape in the roast chicken sold at the corner, the liquor pooled in clay bowls, the gold trinkets woven into hair, the red strings knotted around wrists.
They became all those scattered lights burning across the world below the mountain—the brilliant, chaotic tapestry of mortal life.
The roaring gale... Xiao... Feng... Heh, I like that.

She still would not say she liked humans, nor did she wish to play the benevolent deity. But the world below was lively, and she did not mind visiting from time to time... And perhaps, on occasion, she might lend a hand to a few little ones who ventured down the mountain alongside her.
The woman raised her hand and lifted back her cloak. Born and raised by white tigers, she had no name. But since she was entering the mortal world, she might as well do as mortals did—

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Xiaofeng</color>.
